subject: bichir fish
title: Scientists Raised Fish on Land. Their Skeletons Changed

scenes.text: Scientists kept fish out of water for eight months. Their bodies rebuilt themselves.
The bichir is an African fish with gills and lungs. It gulps air through two holes on top of its head.
In 2014, researchers in Canada raised over a hundred young bichirs on a wet mesh floor, with just millimetres of water.
They had to walk on their fins to get around.
The land-raised fish lifted their heads higher, tucked their fins under their bodies and slipped less.
Even their chest bones grew sturdier, a bit like the first fish that crawled onto land.

description:
Bichirs are African fish with both gills and lungs. In a 2014 Nature study, McGill and University of Ottawa researchers raised young bichirs on land for eight months.
The land-raised fish walked more effectively, and their pectoral skeleton changed in ways that resemble early four-legged animals' ancestors.
What should scientists test next?
first_comment: Up to 93 percent of a bichir's air breaths go in through holes on top of its head. Would you keep one?
